purpose: Leflunomide is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis in adults. It helps reduce joint pain, swelling, and stiffness, and can slow down the damage that arthritis causes to your joints over time. It is meant for long-term use to help you feel better and protect your joints.
how_it_works: Leflunomide works by calming down an overactive immune system that is mistakenly attacking your own joints. It blocks certain white blood cells from multiplying, which reduces the inflammation causing your joint pain and damage. Think of it as turning down the volume on the part of your immune system that is causing harm.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, hair thinning, and skin rash. You may also notice mild high blood pressure or elevated liver enzyme levels on your blood tests. Most side effects are manageable but always let your doctor or pharmacist know if something bothers you.
warnings: Leflunomide can cause serious liver problems, so you will need regular blood tests to monitor your liver. It must NOT be taken during pregnancy because it can cause serious birth defects — reliable birth control is essential for both men and women taking this drug. It can also lower your ability to fight infections, so tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, or signs of infection. If you need to stop this medication, a special washout procedure using cholestyramine may be needed to remove it from your body quickly.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg once daily for the first 3 days (a loading dose), followed by a maintenance dose of 10 mg to 20 mg once daily. Your doctor may skip the loading dose to reduce side effects. Always take it at the same time each day, with or without food, and never stop or change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
